contract.application_relevance: Workers construct URL-encoded event submissions from a reusable parameter object.
contract.cleanup: Every case is awaited before cleanup. Track explicit readers and body streams; cancel/release readers, initiate all unlocked-stream cancellations before joining them, and retain no request-local objects. Buffered body producers may be lazy; explicit JS stream producers are finite and close synchronously. Cleanup records runtime-retained locks with awaited consumer/descendant proof, and any unverified lock blocks acceptance. No open producer gates, external handles or timers are used. Await both Y220 consumers with allSettled. If a body method or cleanup does not settle within the external deadline, supervisor terminates only the owned process group and records failure/unknown plus incomplete cleanup. It never reports a pass.
contract.desired_behavior: Media type application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8; body event=launch&count=2; parsed FormData has those two fields.
contract.distinctness: U209/U210 test parameter algorithms directly; this has deliberately plain values and tests the Request/Body integration seam and snapshot.
fixed_runtime_assertions: t.equal(request.headers.get('content-type'), 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8', 'URLSearchParams BodyInit infers its form media type');
t.equal(await t.consume(copy, 'text'), 'event=launch&count=2', 'typed extraction snapshots URLSearchParams serialization');
t.equal(form instanceof FormData, true, 'Body formData dispatch recognizes inferred media type');
t.deep([...form], [['event', 'launch'], ['count', '2']], 'typed body parses to FormData rather than re-reading source params');
t.equal(request.bodyUsed, true, 'form body consumer marks request used');
